title: The ILS in Plain English
hook: Two needles, one runway, zero visibility. Meet the ILS.

scenes.narration: Thirty seconds, kid. The I L S — the precision approach that's been saving bacon since before I had this mustache.

Two beams. The localizer gives you left and right — it's four times more sensitive than a V O R, so fly it with pressure, not heroics. The glideslope gives you up and down, usually a three degree slide to the runway.
Fly both needles centered and a standard Category One I L S takes you to a decision altitude two hundred feet above the touchdown zone, with as little as a half mile visibility.
onScreenText: Vis: as low as ½ SM (RVR 1800)

scenes.narration: At D A you decide: runway environment in sight, land. Not in sight? Missed approach. There's no 'take a peek' option, kid. The glideslope doesn't care about your dinner reservation.
Localizer left-right, glideslope up-down, two hundred and a half, decide at D A. Chase the needles gently — they bite back near the ground.
A I M one dash one dash nine has every beam, marker, and mile. Bring coffee.

quiz.question: Standard Category I ILS minimums are:
choices: DA 200 ft HAT, visibility ½ SM / RVR 1,800
quiz.explanation: A standard CAT I ILS goes down to 200 ft above touchdown with as little as ½ SM or RVR 1,800 (AIM 1-1-9; exact values are on the plate).

quiz.question: Compared to a VOR course, the localizer is:
choices: About 4x more sensitive — small corrections only
quiz.explanation: The localizer's full-scale deflection is roughly a quarter of a VOR's, so needle movements are faster — correct with small pressures.

quiz.question: Reaching DA without the runway environment in sight, you must:
choices: Level off at DA and continue to the MAP
quiz.explanation: DA is a decision altitude — no runway environment means missed approach, beginning at DA. (91.175)
